original_test_intent: Read the intended BMC's SessionService resource, validate its service identity, Sessions link and approved service-level configuration metadata, and preserve a redacted snapshot without enumerating or changing active sessions.
original_method: Retain one GET to `/redfish/v1/SessionService`, reject DeepSeek's individual-session substitution, and replace embedded credentials/TLS bypass with trusted least-privilege access and SessionService schema validation.
manual_activity: The BMC/security owner confirms that this row is limited to SessionService metadata, approves the credential/certificate trust and defines which service configuration, timeout, links and OEM fields may be retained.
required_inputs: BMC endpoint bound to immutable SUT identity
Field-level redaction and secure raw evidence policy
safety_requirements: Do not expose credentials, tokens or Authorization
Do not append a session ID
Do not follow or enumerate Sessions members
Redact security-sensitive timeout/OEM data as approved
No session creation/deletion or log clearing
agent_execution_scope: Validate Sessions collection link without following it
Compare approved service properties to baseline
Export redacted snapshot and no-mutation audit
engineer_actions: Resolve service-versus-session scope and approve access
Provide expected service property/link baseline and redaction

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The command is inapplicable: it targets one `/Sessions/<id>` member and emits username/origin IP, while the Master targets `/SessionService`. It also uses TLS bypass and unsafe basic-auth handling.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With approved certificate trust and secret-safe least-privilege authentication, GET exactly https://<BMC>/redfish/v1/SessionService once, validate SessionService @odata/schema and the Sessions link without following it, then export only approved redacted service metadata.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source-exact SessionService endpoint, GET intent and 15/10 timing remain; no session ID or member metadata is imported.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat this as a service-capability/configuration check: verify trusted transport, exact SessionService identity, link shape and approved timeout/service fields while explicitly excluding the active-session collection and members.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds schema/baseline and safe evidence controls and removes DeepSeek's wrong member scope.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: This row validates service-level metadata and the existence/shape of the Sessions link; the next row separately inventories the collection, and neither authorizes reading an individual session.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: SessionService configuration and OEM fields may disclose security posture. Following the link or appending an ID would expand privacy scope and change testcase identity.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish SDK is equivalent only if it requests exactly SessionService, preserves certificate binding, does not auto-expand links, performs the same schema/property checks and applies approved redaction.
expected_evidence: Credential-provider and parser/schema versions without secrets
HTTP status/content type and access-controlled raw response hash
Sessions link validation without member access

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master item, path and command consistently require GET /SessionService, while the same-row DeepSeek command replaces it with /SessionService/Sessions/<SESSION_ID> and exposes member fields. These are different Redfish resources and coverage scopes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Master resource is explicit and can be executed after the owner confirms that authoritative service-only scope and supplies trust, access, schema and redaction prerequisites.

review_improvement: Rejects the wrong individual-session substitution and defines a bounded SessionService schema/link check that cannot silently expand into active-session disclosure.
independent_technical_reasoning: SessionService is a singleton describing session management capability/configuration and linking to the Sessions collection; a Session member instead represents one active authentication context with privacy-sensitive user and origin data. Substituting the latter neither tests the source endpoint nor preserves risk scope. Exact @odata.id, schema and link validation can cover the Master intent without following the collection, and service fields should still be redacted according to the approved security baseline.
